Cameron Winter has 15x fewer Spotify listeners than Troye Sivan (1.4M vs 21.1M), and more people rated his new album: 3,238 ratings vs 2,680. 🎹

Live at Carnegie Hall, out October 9 on Partisan Records, is the week's most-rated new release on albumoftheyear.org and the best-scored: a 90 user score (3,238 ratings) and an 87 critic score from 12 reviews. It was recorded at Winter's sold-out solo show at Carnegie Hall's Stern Auditorium in December 2025, with reworked songs from his debut Heavy Metal plus three previously unreleased tracks, "It All Fell in the River", "Emperor XIII in Shades" and "If You Turn Back Now". Winter is also the frontman of the band Geese.

The same week: Troye Sivan's fourth album She's the Best landed at a 73 user score (critics: 76 from 13 reviews), and Remi Wolf's Mud at 77 from 1,254 ratings. Critics and fans agreed on Remi Wolf, and fans were a little warmer on Cameron Winter than critics.

The pattern: the album with the smallest audience of the three got the biggest reaction. Ratings count is a rough signal for how many people actually sat down with a record, not just how many follow the artist.

Which album of the week did you actually play start to finish? 👇
